setup.description: Does a restricted member's grant travel to a project he OWNS? userm (uid 100012, created for D5 after the T3 fixture import; the userg-i gap users stay reserved for consumer-side tests) is BOTH 'Feature store restricted' member of usera_project AND Data owner of his own userm_project (id 100006, created by him - proving restricted-elsewhere users can own projects). usera granted him customers_fg ENTIRELY via restrictedaccess (mirror of userk's D2 grant). Crucially, the grant created NO shared_feature_store row for userm_project: restricted_* grants are bound to the user's membership in the producer project and give his own project nothing.

users.userm: uid 100012, restricted member of usera_project + owner of userm_project, granted customers_fg entirely

projects.userm_project: id 100006, userm's own project (store id per feature_store row), empty

context: Design-doc D5 asked how a user with a restricted membership in the producer project is routed when he also holds normal memberships elsewhere. Hypothesis: restricted_* grants are user-scoped to the producer-project membership; project-level shares are the only cross-project route; absent a shared_feature_store/shared_feature_group row for HIS project, the producer store is invisible from his own project's scope.

reads_legend.D5b_fv_in_own_project_over_usera_fg: same scope; attempt create_feature_view in userm's OWN store over usera_customers_fg columns
reads_legend.D5c_usera_project_scope_parity_with_F4: hsfs login project=usera_project (his restricted membership); fetch both FGs' metadata

description: MEASURED: a restricted user's grants are exercisable ONLY inside the producer project. Owning another project changes nothing for cross-project access - the producer store is not even listed from his own project (404/270008, A2 parity), so an FV over the producer's FGs can never be created in his own store. Inside usera_project he behaves exactly like userk (F4): granted FG metadata ok, ungranted FG 400/270266.

grants.shared_feature_store_rows_for_userm_proj: NONE - the restricted grant created no store share for his project

D5a_own_project_reach_usera_store.usera_store: denied: HTTP 404, errorCode 270008, 'Featurestore wasn't found.' (usrMsg: featurestoreName: usera_project_featurestore , project: userm_project)

D5b_fv_in_own_project_over_usera_fg.fv_creation: denied at store resolution: HTTP 404, errorCode 270008 - the foreign FG can never be referenced from his own project, so no FV over it can exist in his own store

D5c_usera_project_scope_parity_with_F4.transactions_fg: denied: HTTP 400, errorCode 270266, 'The feature group is not shared' (identical to userk's F4 probe)

D5d_fv_catalog_listing.userm: items=[userk_own_fv] count=4 - sees ANOTHER user's FV because its constituent features (customers only) fit his grant; creator irrelevant
D5d_fv_catalog_listing.userk: items=[userk_own_fv] count=4 - even the creator's view is grant-filtered, not ownership-based: userl_own_fv (references num_transactions_30d) is hidden from him
D5d_fv_catalog_listing.userj: items=[] count=4 - no grants, empty list, but the TOTAL FV count of the store leaks (same loose-metadata family as the prepared-statement leak)
D5d_fv_catalog_listing.conclusion: no per-FV ACL: catalog visibility for restricted members = the recursive constituent-feature check applied per FV
